changes.before: Replace continue with break. What prints?
changes.after: continue skips the rest of one loop turn. break ends the loop.

before: for (int i=0; i<4; i++) initializes once, tests before each body and updates after a completed body. i++ adds one.
continue starts the next iteration; in this for loop, the update still happens before the next condition test.
break leaves the loop immediately instead of moving to its next iteration.
The small counter and fixed limit make every increment representable. A syntactic loop alone does not guarantee termination.

Expected output or behavior: 0
2
3. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Trace initialization,test,body,update separately for both versions. Do not use an unbounded overflow loop. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A for loop has a start, a test, and an update. Here i starts at 0. The loop checks `i < 4` before each turn. `i++` adds 1 after the turn.
`continue` skips the rest of the current turn. In this for loop, the update still happens. Then the next test decides whether another turn can begin.
`break` leaves the loop immediately. It skips both the rest of the turn and this loop's next update.
The counter takes only small values here. When i reaches 4, the test becomes false. Always check that your loop can reach its stopping point without exceeding a number's range.
The loop prints 0, skips the print when i is 1, then prints 2 and 3. Each number appears on its own line.
Replace continue with break. Follow i from 0 and stop as soon as the break runs.
